notes.title: EA Hotfix 1.0
notes.content:
[i][b]Hello Captains, new and old![/b][/i]

Firstly just wanted to say a massive, massive thank you for your kind words, support and understanding on Early Access Launch! We've said this a bunch before, but launching a game is not easy, especially not as an indie -- and the community has been so warm and understanding. Thank you so much, again, from the bottom of our hearts.

In the first 48 hours of launch, we've received over 500 reports to our In-Game Bug Reporter, 150+ reports to our Community Discord and 300+ in the Steam Forums. These bits of information are so integral not only to squelch bugs, but to validate our suspicions and ideas for the future. The great part is that most of these pieces of feedback, suggestions and bugs are right up in the forefront of our minds, and we're actively working hard on solutions.

Early Access is never easy! But we are confident that this hotfix that should ease some really core problems in gameplay.

[b]The biggest implementation (other than the save game fixes) is that we’ve implemented some new Officer Orders for resource processing and power generation. [/b]This should hopefully help alleviate some of those priority issues folks were having. We’re going to keep adding to these features as the game progresses in Early Access.

[h3]Save Games[/h3]
[list]
[*] Some community members would experience a frustrating bug where Save Games could break after sending out an Away Mission. This should be reconciled with this hotfix.
[*] We’ve solved a whole host of bugs that were corrupting save files. There were a few issues causing it, so this is a bit of a catch-all, but we are Hopeful that we have squashed them all.
[*] The bug that occurred when saves would be saved to a single save slot – thus resulting in every save reloading the same game – should be resolved now.
[*] You should now be able to select any save slot from the Pause Menu! Huzzah!
[*] The team have made improvements to visualizations of Save Games: new games should now appear at the top, older games at the bottom, Pause Menu strings have been resolved, excessive amounts of save files have been reduced, etc.
[*] Sometimes players would exit the Main Menu from the End Game Screen, resulting in the game inadvertently saving and causing a Failed Load state. This should also be resolved!
[*] We saw a few game crashes in the asteroid belt – this should not occur anymore.[/list]

[h3]Away Missions[/h3]
[list]
[*] The bug that prevented players from recalling a Shuttle when multiple Away Missions were launched should be resolved now.
[*] When the Hangar lost power, Shuttles could become stuck in departing for their Mission. This should not occur anymore!
[*] Shuttles have become stuck because Crew couldn’t/wouldn’t depart for their Mission. We still have more investigating to do, but you should be able to Recall a Mission and see the crew become unstuck.
[/list]

[h3]Misc. Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] We’ve improved the game balancing slightly so that the starting resources are more generous - we know this is not a total fix but while we work on a longer term solution this will hopefully alleviate some of the resource issues.
[*] We’ve changed up the deconstruction costs of build mode - it will no longer incur a fee to move things.
[*] We’ve fixed an issue where some online services starting up were causing issues with authentication, both for Feedback and also for the Twitch Integration. If you were having issues with either, they should be fixed now.
[*] We’ve fixed the issue where the crew were deciding to start a Moshpit instead of getting to work.
[*] The frustrating bug where the Feedback Form would not display to some users should be all fixed! You should see it on the right hand side of your screen.
[*] There were reports of keyboard + mouse controls becoming unresponsive at some points in gameplay, making it impossible to jump forward in a run. This shouldn’t occur anymore!
[*] We have fixed an issue where tooltips were getting stuck when hovered over.
[*] Sometimes, Crew tooltips/statuses lingered too long, even after the Status was alleviated. This shouldn’t occur anymore!
[*] We’ve fixed a couple of pathfinding issues with the crew - we don’t feel like it has completely solved pathfinding, but it should be more rare now. We’ll continue working away on this one.
[*] At times, the Zutopan Combat didn’t reload properly, and the Zutopans didn’t get their weapons back. While this is ideal for your Crew, it’s definitely not the intended experience – and should be resolved now.
[*] For those that were experiencing issue with infinite load screens, you should no longer have issues with that.
[*] The team have made visual improvements to Game UI and Localisation - again this is a step towards a bigger fix in the longer term.
[/list]

[h1]Some Important Notes[/h1]
[b]With this Patch, some testers using Custom Runs in canonical layouts have seen an extreme amount of fire. We’re working on a solution to this, but in the meantime, we suggest you stay clear of that layout unless you wish for extra-crispy crew.[/b]

Another note to keep in mind - if you set an Order Priority and then save and reload, that priority currently won’t load back in. We’re aware and actively working on a fix.

You can also expect a Patch in the next week intended to address the larger, less-critical bugs in gameplay. We'll have more information very soon, but not just yet -- our priorities are actively shifting based on what we hear from players, and as a small team, we're making important decisions on functional gameplay, team bandwidth and critical issues.

[i][b]The first big Content Update will come within the next 6-8 weeks and will be called A Dangerous Galaxy…. [/b][/i]

We've also had a lot of questions about our intentions and ideas for the future! We will have some news about that next week too, along with a streamed Q + A to chat with you all about the vision we have for the game.

Thanks again for all of your support and patience, it genuinely means the world to us!

Keeping your Hope Bars full,

<3 LoG

Four years later in 2021, with active support on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/290340/Armello/]Armello[/url] wrapping up and having cancelled an unannounced project, under the working title ‘Loveboat Yamato’… development began in earnest on our “starship adventure sim.”

With fingers crossed and our eyes on the Forever Star, we genuinely hope Jumplight Odyssey resonates with you all. If it truly does, the best way you can support an indie team like ours is to give the game a positive review and share it far and wide. It really does make a difference.

notes.title: EA is Only 4 Days Out! It's Time to Rally! 📣
notes.content:
Hey Spacefarers!

We’re right on the precipice of Jumplight Odyssey’s launch into Early Access. It is now just four days away. 

After years of ideation, brainstorming, implementation and troubleshooting… We’re finally at a point that we can hand over the Captain reigns to you, the community.

That’s not to say the game is finished or perfect. Bugs are an explicit part of the game development process, and considering we are still deep in development, we are entering Early Access knowing that certain issues exist. However, it is your feedback, love and commitment to JLO that will help us shape its future, and we would rather have you all in-game and playing it early, bugs and all, than not at all. 

We’ve said this a hundred times, and those of you from our Armello days will know, but we’re an indie game dev studio based in Melbourne, Australia (we even self-publish our games!). While we’ve been around for over ten years, and we’re very proud of what we’ve accomplished so far, there is still a huge way to go for Jumplight Odyssey’s development. Our vision is clear, but only partly realised.

[b]We’re realistic, but we love to be idealistic, too. We have big hopes for this game and our ambition is way higher than a studio of our size has any right to. This ambition means that we are operating in a space where we are in direct competition with literal publishers with hundreds of millions of dollars.[/b]

([i]Author’s note: We do not have hundreds of millions of dollars.[/i])

And against all odds, Jumplight Odyssey was the 22nd most played game in Next Fest (#2 in Strategy!), we have almost 150,000 wishlists, the impressions from influencers and the press are looking great, and 93% of you surveyed in Next Fest said the experience made you want to purchase the game.  

It is this next part where we turn to you... 

We ask: if you’ve loved Jumplight Odyssey – perhaps you’ve seen some art, played the Demo at Next Fest, watched your favourite streamer play, read an article, etc – that you make some serious noise. [b]There is a time in an indie game’s life cycle where it needs to make some hefty waves to see any success at all – our time is right now. [/b]

[h3]The best way to help us realise our collective dreams with Jumplight Odyssey is to scream about JLO from the rooftops! To show the game to your friends, to your family, to throw it into group chats with people that might love it! Share our [url=https://youtu.be/4k7NmBF3Rdc]early access trailer[/url]. If they (or you) enjoy the game, encourage them to review it on Steam![/h3]

We’re so excited for the future of Jumplight Odyssey and League of Geeks - don’t forget we’re developing [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1893810/Solium_Infernum/]Solium Infernum[/url] as well! 

([i]please do not ask us why we are making two games at once. pls just buy them. we are begging u[/i])

We wish you all could see just how incredibly hard we’ve worked to reach this point today, because you might have a chance at understanding just how grateful we are for all of your love and support so far. 

Let’s make this game take off. 

<3 LoG

notes.content:
[h1]Build Mode on the SDF Catalina![/h1]
[previewyoutube=-X6xPQiCIS0;full][/previewyoutube]
At the heart of each playthrough of Jumplight Odyssey are the Captain’s Build Order decisions… Each little bit of construction aboard the SDF Catalina can have cataclysmic run-on effects, no matter how small the decision might feel! Whether that be your decision to build a Radar Amplifier rather than new Pistol Lockers, or prioritizing an efficient Manufacturing Bay over Produce and Crew Meals -- your decisions [i][b]really do count[/b][/i] as you navigate through the stars!

From the Demo, we saw a variety of Captain prioritization come into play. For some Captains, they will prioritize Metals, Composites and Manufacturing, other Captains are quick on expanding their Jumplight capabilities down in the Engine Rooms, and other Captains seek to stabilize any problems in the Water and Produce supply chains…

Ultimately, part of the magic of the SDF Catalina is the incredible run-on effects to a playthrough that can occur from Build Mode!

[h3]Customize Layouts, Create new Rooms, Decorate your Ship in Build Mode[/h3]
Whether you’re feeling more comfy or strategic or somewhere in between, the SDF Catalina can be built out to your exact specifications. The layout of your ship is completely up to your imagination (well – there are some rooms that are bespoke and cannot be customized – but most of it is yours!)

For Early Access, there are over 10 different rooms for you to build out. Each room possesses their own specialty furniture and equipment, and serves an integral function to the ship. They are all important, but what to prioritize is completely up to you as the Captain.

[h3]Optimize your Systems to Keep your Crew and Ship Running[/h3]
As with any functional starship, building is not always about aesthetics – it is a cornerstone of survival strategy. In pursuit of survival among the stars, crew efficiency and resource management are the name of the game! 

Some Captains prefer to run the defensive and maximise the amount of time in each Biome by building out Small Weapons Lockers, Helmet Lockets and Medikits. Thus, when the Zutopans board, they can hang out long enough for their Away Missions to return before Jumping away! Other Captains prefer complete evasion – decking out their Jumplight Calibrators and Cartridges to ensure they’re always well ahead of the Zutopans. 

For the Captains that prefer to engage more casually, they focus on creating a happy, inviting atmosphere aboard – lots of Recreational Rooms and facilities for Crew to hang out in (and for juicy, juicy drama to go down)…

[h3]Even Space is a Resource in Space! Utilize it Effectively[/h3]
While the SDF Catalina is huge, it is not boundless… You only have a certain amount of room to make your lofty ambitions work. Being able to integrate space with function and design will be a hallmark of a great Captain! The Catalina is a huge Cruiser, but the more that you play, the more folks you’ll find along the way, the more mouths to feed, the more chaos will occur! 

We’re so excited for you all to experience the epic highs and lows of Jumplight Odyssey…

And the SDF Catalina awaits your architectural touch, Captain! The only word of warning we have is to be wary of the Building-Bottleneck – it occurs when you build too fast and hard to begin!

[h1]Crew Relationships (the DRAMA!)[/h1]
[previewyoutube=jhdlBcVgn9k;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Building Strong Relationships with your Crew is Crucial…[/h3]
The Odyssey of JLO isn’t just about piloting a ship through the stars: it’s also about navigating the relationships and messy, messy drama that forms among your crew members! In this universe, where survival quite literally hinges on unity, building strong connections with your crew is a key factor in your success as a Captain. Also… Who doesn’t want to know the tea? :frog: :tea: 

[h3]Your Crew are Unique: They Have Personalities and Motivations![/h3]
Each crew member in JLO is more than a mere face on the ship. They are individuals that each have distinct personalities, with their own fun quirks and motivations, feelings and moods! It is these attributes that affect their interactions, and the interactions between crew that can make or break a starship!

[h3]There’s Friendships, Crushes, Rivalries, Unrequited Feelings…[/h3]
When navigating through each of the information panels of your crew, you can uncover a juicy myriad of interpersonal drama. By just scrolling around the Catalina, you can spot friendships blossoming, rivalries igniting, crushes forming – all right before your very eyes! But – just like in real life – not every connection is reciprocated. Unrequired feelings may add some tension to the already-fragile emotional tapestry!

[h1]Beware the Zutopans![/h1]
[previewyoutube=cVJcXKYTjOk;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]A Relentless Threat[/h3]
For those Captains up for the challenge of being pursued by the Zutopans, be warned! They are an arrogant, warmongering people, led by the worst of them all: Admiral Voltan. The Zutopans will not just stop at destroying your home world, once known as Pleiades, but will seek the SDF Catalina out remorselessly as you flee throughout the stars!

(Again, you can play with the Zutopans switched off!)

[h3]Admiral Voltan is Prepared to Hunt You Down[/h3]
The SDF Catalina and its crew are no strangers to danger at this point. The entire ship is calibrated defensively to hold off encroaching boarding pods long enough for the Captain to command a Jump. With eyes fixed on the radar, and a racing heart, it's assured you'll be counting down the seconds to get-the-hell-out-of-there!

In the face of an enemy that knows no respite, your role as the Captain of the SDF Catalina is one that calls for tough decision-making. With each leap into the unknown, you forge the ship's path to the ever-elusive Forever Star, but Admiral Voltan is never too far away... 

We're so close to EA now!

Keeping your Hope Bars Full,

<3 LoG

notes.title: The Runway to EA! 🌌All Hands on Deck!
notes.content:
[h1]Gardening & Cooking on the SDF Catalina![/h1]

[previewyoutube=yx5laLEsGMw;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Bring your Farm to the Stars in the Greenhouse ✨[/h3]
Life still needs to be nurtured within the stars! The Greenhouse is your plant care hub, housing an oasis of greenery and herbs. Your Scientists will tend to the crops, nurturing them from saplings to harvest. Then, Supply will deliver the Produce to the Kitchen, where it will be cooked up and served as meals in the Cafeteria!

[h3]Supply Food and Oxygen for Your Ship[/h3]
The Greenhouse is a cosy, ambient place for your crew to hangout, but it also serves a vital purpose! You are able to choose between a variety of plants and plant-growing stations – some will grow more slowly but have higher yield, others are quick sprouters but don’t produce as much per harvest.

The plants also have a hand in producing oxygen aboard your ship!

[h3]Keep Your Crew Nourished After a Long Shift[/h3]
After being harvested and stored by Scientists, the Produce is then transported and cooked up for the rest of the crew by Supply. When off shift or their needs are dire, your crew will meander over to the cafeteria and enjoy some of the prepared meals.

[h1]Jumplight & The Engine on the SDF Catalina[/h1]

[previewyoutube=PCuEP2VPLiI;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Your Ship Runs on Jumplight Stored in the Engine Room![/h3]
In your Odyssey, the very essence propelling you comes from the stars themselves! Through a meticulous and super secret process, starlight is harnessed into the wondrous Jumplight Engine (RGB ball go brrr!). Jumplight is then measured in the top left of your UI screen. When you have a target Biome locked in, you can see exactly how much Jumplight you’ll need to acquire.

[h3]Upgrades let you Travel Farther and Gain Jumplight Faster[/h3]
Like stars, your journey isn’t static! By focusing on building out Upgrades in the Engine Room, you’re able to employ a variety of improvements to your engine itself. These enhancements can not only extend your travel range, but also accelerate your acquisition of Jumplight. With six potential upgrade slots, you’ll become the speediest Cruiser ship in the galaxy! And a brief fleck on Voltan’s horizon before you vanish again!

[h3]Initiate the Jumplight Drive from the Bridge to Explore the Galaxy, or Escape the Zutopans![/h3]
Initiate the Jumplight Drive to activate the Engine and Jump successfully. With each Jump, you explore uncharted Biomes, each filled with various, important resources, survivors requiring rescue and other strange encounters! 

But the power of the Jumplight Drive isn't confined to exploration alone. In moments of urgency, when the Zutopan Fleet's ominous shadow looms large, the Drive becomes your lifeline. Earn enough Jumplight to escape each time, or risk being boarded by the Zutopans.

[h1]Away Missions![/h1]

[previewyoutube=OP5SadiYTjA;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Away Missions Play a Vital Role in Keeping Your Ship Running[/h3]
While your attention will remain on the SDF Catalina as the Captain, a large part of the everyday function of the ship is to send off Away Missions with your crew. These expeditions are integral to your survival – it is out in the cosmos that your crew will uncover new resources, opportunities and – sometimes – challenges, too!

[h3]Dispatch Away Missions From Your Hangar to Scout Biomes, Survey Planets, Gather Resources and Rescue Civilians![/h3]
There are a variety of mission objectives that you can deploy crew with! You can head over to one of our past [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1893820/announcements/detail/3713823860135807808]Developer’s Logs[/url], where we get into the nitty gritty of Away Missions and what they mean! If you want a TL:DR:

🔭 Scout Missions. [i]Gain Intel on Star System, learning its Biome and Missions.[/i]
📝 Survey Missions. [i]Reveal the yield of Resource Missions, expose hidden Salvage Missions.[/i]
💧 Resource Extraction. [i]Gain an amount of a given resources.[/i]
⛑ Rescue Extraction. [i]Gain an amount of Civilians.[/i]
🛦 Combat Air Patrol. [i]Gives early warning of threats for Combat Air Patrol response.[/i]

[h3]Upgrade and Build new Spacecraft to Explore Farther and Scout for Threats[/h3]
As you traverse the galaxy, a very tempting option is to focus on building out new Spacecraft. These vessels come in a diverse array, each with their own benefits and drawbacks worth considering. You can find more information on the Shuttles in the aforementioned [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1893820/announcements/detail/3713823860135807808]Developer’s Log[/url]!

[h3]But Keep an Eye on the Time, or you may Have to Jump Before Your Crew Returns![/h3]
To send out an Away Mission is to take a chance on those crewmembers not returning – a super scary thought for any Captain! At times, they do not return as a result of Mission Failure. Often, though, you are caught in a predicament where the Zutopans are oppressively on your doorstep, and the Away Missions are not returning any time soon… Meaning the hard decision to be made is to preserve the lives of the crew onboard and to Jump away, leaving your Shuttle stranded.

[b][i]Ultimately, there’s plenty to do in Jumplight Odyssey, and you can hop in on the action come August 21, when Early Access goes LIVE![/i][/b]

Keeping your Hope Bar Full,

LoG

notes.title: Developer's Log #7: A Glimpse into Game Design (Q&A Answers)
notes.content:
Greetings again Spacefarers! 🚀

We hope that you’ve been loving the Demo. It’s been incredible seeing all of your playthroughs and vicariously enjoying your best (and most stressful moments) on the SDF Catalina!

This Developer’s Log is an update that references heavily into the recent [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=66wzF4sW7-0]Jumplight Odyssey Game Design Q&A[/url] with our Principal Game Designer, Felix. It also addresses a lot of the questions we’ve seen pop up in the community over the course of the Demo! 

If you’d like to watch the Game Design Stream, you can find the VOD here on our Youtube Channel:

[previewyoutube=66wzF4sW7-0;full][/previewyoutube]
If you wanted to find a recently-updated FAQ, you should hop over to our brand new [url=https://bit.ly/JLO_Steam_FAQ]JLO FAQ Steam Discussion Thread[/url] or hop on into our [url=https://bit.ly/LeagueOfGeeksDiscord]Official Discord Server[/url]! You can hang out there with our Community Managers who will happily answer whatever questions you have! 💕

[h1]Releasing the Demo[/h1]
Before we hop into the details, we wanted to take the time to really express our gratitude for all of the JLO love! The team were quite nervous to present our first public-facing version of gameplay (rightfully so!), but other than a few resolvable problems, the reception was overwhelmingly positive! 

So thank you! We have heard all of your feedback, gathered information from the recent survey and are in top-secret development discussions as you read. We'll be working hard to create the best version of JLO into Early Access and beyond! 🫡

[i]Now, for your regularly scheduled programming…[/i]

[h1]A Confluence of Genres[/h1]
So much of the challenge presented by developing Jumplight Odyssey comes from where it sits at the confluence of a number of different genre spaces. On one side, we’re tapping into life simulation with all of our crew as they exist on the SDF Catalina: each of them have moods, traits, relationships, quirks and – of course – messy, messy drama.

On the other side, we’re tapping into the FTL-like, Oregon Trail-like journey throughout the stars. And, of course, the beating heart of the simulation is the colony sim genre, where we’re running environmental, starship-style simulations for water, power, gravity and oxygen (among other things!). 

Much of the development complexity emerges when we work to have these genres speak to each other. Where we let the genres interlace, but not overshadow, one another. Our Game Director, Blake, often likes to refer to the game as “[i]a machine that has two halves[/i]”. One half is that hardcore environmental simulation, and the other half is the soap opera drama aboard the ship. If one half isn’t speaking to the other in any given system – if there’s no throughput or points of connectivity – it’s not working for us. So much of what the SDF Catalina is capable of presents itself through the crew. This is why it is integral from a Game Design perspective that we use the crew members to reflect back to the Captain (you, the player) the state of the ship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/f13cdc83d1f72540b655b80eb7766c0a94b470de.gif[/img]

This brings rise to the question: “[i][b]how can you possibly be aware of everything all the time?[/b][/i]”

And the answer is: [i][b]you don’t need to be, because the most important things will be surfaced to you![/b][/i] While not necessarily yet reflected in JLO's Demo, eventually communication with your Officers will serve as a vital information thoroughfare. 

You’ll also receive supplement information through several UI elements! The HUD (Heads Up Display) provides intel on any critical statuses affecting the ship. It is intended to be a “late warning indicator”, but also functions as a useful overview of what is systemically going wrong aboard your ship. 

While there certainly will be Captains that play at this eagle-eye level, we also recognize that there will be players in JLO who want to go and check/optimize absolutely everything -- and that's totally fine as well! That's why we let you pause time.

Ultimately, it's integral to us at LoG that we're crafting a game that lets you test and experiment with diverse playstyles to find your favourite! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/51f202f698f4f82af10a2aba38185d94e4ebda9b.gif[/img]

[h1]The Importance of Your Crew[/h1]
While you will likely receive a lot of vital information from your Officers, it’s worth noting that if you zoom around your ship, you can also observe how your crew are feeling by watching the specific members. If someone is sad or downtrodden, they will work with their head bowed. If they are injured, they will walk with a limp. If someone is getting low on hygiene, a small stink trail follows them wherever they go. It’s these subtle – or not so subtle, in stinky-crew’s case – cues that show the uniqueness of each crew member. They operate with moods, influences and needs just like regular people. Getting this detail to the current level of polish was one of the big challenges that we had to solve, so we’re very proud of the result!

A different use-case of how this organic decision-making space is exemplified in gameplay is the various [i][b]Alert Systems[/b][/i] aboard. We’ve covered off on these in detail in a [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1893820/announcements/detail/3675547274682012887]Past Developer’s Log[/url] if you wanted some context! 

Moving into [i][b]Yellow Alert 🟡[/b][/i] means that work is completed more quickly. It also won’t actively cause Stress to your crew, because it’s not one of the battle stations. But it does force everyone to be On Duty. What Yellow Alert means is that, sure, they are going to be working, but when they’re working, they’re not looking after their Needs. So, over time, people are going to start to get tired. They’ll get hungry. They won’t be able to socialize as much, so they’ll start to feel isolated. 

([i]You might've seen the result of a crew member not taking care of their Needs if you've sent crew on an Away Mission, and they've collapsed as soon as they exited the Shuttle![/i])

A lot of the Captain’s decisions are systemic by nature. The more that you play Jumplight Odyssey, the more you can see the interconnectivity of these systems, the more that you’ll learn how “hard” you can push your crew and the interesting outcomes that arrive. The trade-off in Yellow Alert is get the construction done, but at the cost of wearing your crew out completely.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/8652d804e770d180ed5907504d1f7a991200d394.gif[/img]

The Catalina doesn’t run without the crew, and the crew can’t survive without the Catalina. For example, the Catalina provides essential life support such as water, oxygen and gravity that keep crew alive, but these systems will begin to break down without crew to operate and maintain them.

There’s a co-dependency between divisions as well! We have four divisions that we split the staffing into: Supply, Science, Combat and Engineering. Each of these Divisions has separate responsibilities but no Division is an island; they all depend on each other in various ways to work together as one cohesive, organic ecosystem.

An example is the simple act of being able to serve food for crew to eat in the cafeteria! To do so, you need to grow crops, and Scientists tend to those crops. After the crops have grown, the food that comes out of it needs to be hauled to the kitchen by Supply. The kitchen will cook and serve the food for everyone to eat. This is just a really simple example of two divisions working alongside each other, but as many of you have found, there are far more complex resource chains that stretch across all divisions. 

[h3]Improvements in Crew for EA![/h3]
The survey and community feedback gave strong indication that you would love to see better UI/UX, Crew Management, Prioritization and Hauling. We’re very excited to say that we’re working on all of these facets of gameplay – it’s very important for us to get this right. Come EA, we hope to have an iteration that gets everybody really excited, and have plans to continue to hone the experience even further with input from the community beyond our EA launch!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/b56365dab6b7ecd1b3cc33012b88eeee4e827fde.gif[/img]

[h1]What are “Captain’s Promises”?[/h1]
This is where we’re going to have to be particularly coy… This is a gameplay system currently under development, but we wanted to hint at it during the Demo. Some of you with very keen eyes have spotted the tab that says “[i][b]Captain’s Promises[/b][/i]” in Captain Euphora’s Chambers.

The main hint that we’ll give is in reference to the “Hope Bar”. By hovering over the Hope Bar, you can see there is talk on Promises and their place in the gameplay system. 

[h3]What is Hope?[/h3]
Hope is the measure of the SDF Catalina’s overall outlook and belief in you as their Captain. Hope declines when crew die or are left behind, and increase when a promise is fulfilled or survivors are collected (among other things). Hope is a particularly powerful tool for a Captain because it directly influences the Morale of all of your crew.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/2d26ead84d8ed63b8d7ff5121026fc1dc57b5c3b.png[/img]

Every crew member has a Morale Bar that indicates how well they’re doing. If someone has really low Morale, it will trend up over time toward Hope. If a crew member’s Morale Bar is completely depleted, they’ll fall into “Despair” (previously called “Broken”). This status creates particularly volatile emotional states, and means they’ll stop work, sleep in, among other problematic behaviours. There are a few Despair habits that have debuted in the Demo – one of which is the Pyromaniac, who will go ahead and light fires throughout the ship, yelling “[i][b]it all has to BURN![/b][/i]”. So… Safe to say that Hope is a valuable tool for a Captain.

Euphora’s promise is “No one Left Behind”, so the ship gains Hope every time a civilian is rescued.

We’re not quuiiiiteee ready to share how the Promise system works, but safe to say… It’s very intimately tied to Hope.

Speaking of survivors…

[h1]Will we be Able to Train the Survivors?[/h1]
The short answer is: not in the Demo, no! Who’s to say about the future plans… 👀

In the current Demo, survivors are brought aboard your ship and become Civilians (their own “Division”). They don’t contribute to work, will eat your food and breathe your oxygen… But they’re actively contributing to the social sphere of the ship. They can have relationships and boost other people’s Morale. If you can manage to get your civilians inspired, they’ll walk around inspiring others.

They’re existing as a vibe ✨ for now. We do have plans on integrating civilians into crew, but we can’t say much here just yet… 

[h1]Who are the Custom Characters in the Key Art?[/h1]
The Key Art on Steam and around our Social Media shows off some special-looking characters… While we can’t give much away, we can confirm that we certainly have plans for more bespoke characters like Euphora within the JLO Universe. They will coexist with all of these procedurally generated crew and interact with them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/a74fb8cbd403a603de0759843a6d6adedb57d7e8.png[/img]

More to come here! Watch this space 😉

[h1]Does That Mean There is a Running Universal Storyline?[/h1]
It’s very important to us that you feel, as the Captain, that you are telling [i]YOUR[/i] story. But we also – especially with Euphora’s Odyssey – want to make sure that our IP and universe has a beating heart, with a greater narrative unfolding. It’s best described as playing “shades of Euphora”. You are following her canonical journey, but there’s lots of procedural generation that goes into everything – your crew, your biomes, even Euphora herself! So no one’s run will be the same as anyone else’s. Events may occur in your run that would never occur in your friend’s, and vice versa.

[h3]Jumplight Odyssey is a “Colony Sim With Rogue-Like Elements”[/h3]
We’ve said a few times before that Jumplight Odyssey is best described as a “colony sim with rogue-lite elements”. We’ve just explored the procedural generation above, and how everything is completely unique to your run. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/beff982e138e2d59a4f9a22fae1b00fd77ed9f20.gif[/img]

Another facet of the rogue-lite elements we’ve integrated into JLO are what Felix, our Principal Game Designer, likes to call “[i]Compounding Decision Space[/i]”. Making a decision in the first half hour of the game, then making another decision half an hour later that adds weight to the initial decision and so on. You can find really great examples of this Compounding Decision-making in the Boons available from Hades, or the deck-building in Slay the Spire. 

[b]While we can’t discuss everything that we’re dying to show off, we can confirm that there are plans for systems that expand the compounding decision-making players will experience in JLO.[/b]

There is a small glimpse into this decision-making when entering certain Biomes. Some Biomes have adverse effects like “[i]Gravitational Pull[/i]”. These situations are a perfect example of the procedural generation creating interesting emergent gameplay. As a player, you then learn: “oh damn, if I go to this particular biome, I have to plan for that, because my Away Missions are going to be slower.” 

These are the moments where there’s a wrench thrown in the works and you have to adapt on your feet. This is when you really come into your stead as a Captain of the SDF Catalina. Perhaps, the first time, these moments lead to colony collapse and complete disaster, but in the next run, you’re ready this time. There’s lots of learning involved in mastering Jumplight Odyssey, linking both colony sims and roguelites in learning from failure and trying again.

[b]It’s also worth noting that for saving and loading, we’re adopting the structure of a colony sim, not of a hardcore roguelite. You’ll be able to save and load your game.[/b]

This is not in the Demo, but is planned for EA. So if you reach a point of no return, there’s an abysmal failure and you can see it coming, you can reload from your last save!

[h1]Will There be Different Modes Available?[/h1]
There will be Custom Odysseys, absolutely. You will be able to define a number of parameters so that you can set up a run in the various ways that you want to play Jumplight Odyssey. [b]You are more than able to play a more chilled version of JLO than presented in the Demo.[/b] There are options to remove the pressure of the Zutopan Fleet all together and just chill, or dial that pressure up even further!

More to come here!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/898ab149abd922a262c14d4c5b9316550519ca32.gif[/img]

[h1]Will There be Variations on Combat Intensity?[/h1]
What we have playable in the current Demo is a very solid foundation for combat. The feeling that we intend to evoke with JLO’s combat is – yes, this is a battle cruiser, and it is a military vessel – but this is not a war game, and you are not playing a Captain who is trying to win battles. You’re playing a Captain that is trying to survive, and to preserve the last of her people by taking them to their safety – the Forever Star. It is really important to us that the first version of combat – the one that you experience in the Demo – elicits the feeling that this pursuing Zutopan fleet are dangerous. They should feel oppressive.

Ultimately, the fact that you can only hope to survive and jump away is a very fundamental part of our combat Game Design. That’s not to say that we won’t have more varieties of combat in the future, it was just important for us to build the “Zutopan Fleet are scary” foundation tonally in this Demo. 

[h1]Should we Expect any Other Threats? Or can I Just Speedrun to the Forever Star?[/h1]
Once we move beyond the Demo, you will be able to play further through the journey screen. After some time, you may start to see the repercussions of skipping stars accumulate. Skipping biomes means skipping over resources – there is an attached [i]opportunity cost[/i]. It is a sense that you will hone in as your experience as Captain grows, you will find that you know which resources are worth skipping and which are worth hanging around for, even with the Zutopans at your backdoor. 

There may also be other threats that you’ll need to factor for, and start building toward early… But that’s information for another time. 😉

[h1]Could you give some examples of maybe what might unlock as you progress?[/h1]
Those with keen eyes have noticed that in some of our shopping lists, when you are putting together rooms and selecting items, they are grouped into different tiers which are unlocked by various objects. So – essentially a tech tree of sorts – that works throughout the shopping list system

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/ccfd813fe68efa9cc18f9fcd4b3f2561e644ea1d.gif[/img]

So, you might need to build Object A to access Objects B, C and D. Then Object D unlocks access to further objects… 

([i]Worth noting that these unlock chains can be broken if objects go offline, which can cause ‘cascade failure’ throughout the ship.[/i])

At least, this is one form of upgrading. These upgrades are also the way more, run-defining upgrades that will help you hone the build of your ship. We hope to grow this list out past EA, though there are some in the Demo that you can play around with! 

Another form of progression are upgrades to the key areas of your ship; your Bridge, Flight Control Center and Engine Room. These are finite slots with limited space.

More to come here!

[h1]What Kind of Customization Could you Speak to in JLO, Now or in the Future?[/h1]
Ever since the conception of the game, we've been talking about customization and giving players option to customize. It’s worth noting that we are an indie team, so we do have to be very cautious about what we commit ourselves to.

So for the time being, and probably for Early Access, we don't plan to have any player facing customization. But that's not to say that we won't do it in the future!

That's the beauty of Early Access. It's a way for us to get a really strong foundation out there, to get people playing JLO and to listen to our community. We can gauge what you are enjoying, what you’re not enjoying, what you're wanting and what you don't want.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/3625353e9815c29f99a86725386fbd82a17feee8.gif[/img]

Having EA really helps us to make those decisions around allocating scope and budget, etc.. Because we are an indie company, we have to be very cautious with our time. We can't do everything, especially not at the level of polish that we want to see in the game totally. So it's one of those things that is we're actively watching to see how much people want it.

[h1]Will There Be a Way to Beef up Ham?[/h1]
There's definitely been talk in the studio about how viable is a run where you invest heavily into Ham.

So much of Game Design is about providing tools for the player to tell their own goofy stories. And so we've already seen people in the demo do some crazy stuff… And that fills our hearts with so much joy, because ultimately we're not trying to create one experience. We're trying to create a platform in which people can go and tell their own stories and do kooky little experiments. If you can’t get up to shenanigans in Jumplight Odyssey, we haven't done our job right.

[h3]What's Next?![/h3]
Well… That is everything for now. Again, if you’ve read through this entire post and are still eager – thank you so much! Even though we’re an indie team, we read every comment, piece of feedback and concern brought up. Thank you for playing our Demo, and offering so much love for JLO! 

If you’re wondering “[i][b]What’s Next for JLO!?[/b][/i]”, that’s a question you can find out by hopping in our [url=https://bit.ly/LeagueOfGeeksDiscord]Official Discord Server[/url]! You can chat with other great folks (lots of SciFi commentary!), hang out with our Community Managers in their weekly streams and learn all news first!

We will depart with some of our favourite bugs, mishaps and mischief over the course of the Demo. Please enjoy! And we’ll see you very soon!

notes.title: Developer's Log #6: Zutopan Attack! Combat Trailer Deep Dive
notes.content:
Hold on tight, Spacefarers! 

The [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1893820/announcements/detail/3698064431486525584]Combat Trailer for Jumplight Odyssey has been released[/url], and it’s packed with the chaos and non-stop action of fending off the Zutopan raiding parties.

[previewyoutube=YF_6hqer_9Y;full][/previewyoutube]
You may have caught our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1893820/announcements/detail/3698064431486941979]Combat Analysis Deep Dive Stream[/url] this morning, but if you didn't, don't worry -- we'll be uploading the VOD to Youtube very soon!

Don’t fear, though, this month’s Developer’s Log is going to explore the minutiae of the Trailer, and break down some of this anarchy with Dev insights. ~

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/ab82e8c2fc8be4c61fa7ba015b89e44da42c14a2.gif[/img]

[h2]The Hunt Begins[/h2]
We’re immediately met by Admiral Voltan in his Bridge as he is preparing to launch an attack on the SDF Catalina. Admiral Voltan and his motives have not yet been explored… So far, we know that he is a warmongering leader and commander of the Zutopan forces chasing the SDF Catalina, [i]but there may be some merit in wondering why[/i]…  

[b]Anyway, back to your regular broadcasting!
[/b]
We have reiterated before the importance of the Captain’s decision-making, and there is no tougher decisions than those made when the Catalina is under attack… When the player sounds an [i][b]Alert Level[/b][/i], crew will immediately respond with the corresponding protocol. These are colour-coded, with each Alert Level having its own purpose and intensity (we’ll explore the different Alert Levels later in the Dev Log). But for now, it is important to note that these ‘high’ Alert Levels; Red (Battle Stations) and Magenta (Intruder Alert) include the very important requirement that all Officers and the Captain immediately report to the Bridge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/f13cdc83d1f72540b655b80eb7766c0a94b470de.gif[/img]

Strategic Jumping is your ticket to reaching the Forever Star. While the Captain’s first instinct might be “[i]let’s get the hell out of here[/i]!”, there are other important facets to keep in mind… You might not want to tank the hit to your Hope as a result of losing so many crew to abandoned Away Missions, or maybe you are desperate for the Resources that these Away Missions are bringing back to the Catalina. Perhaps you’re sick of running – for now – and want to face the threat head on. Or, worst of all, you’ve run out of time.

Regardless of your circumstances, the SDF Catalina does come well stocked with a defensive system.

[i][h3]“Princess, the Zutopans will be in our Systems any minute!”[/h3][/i]
You can always check where the Zutopan Forces are by heading to the [b]Star Map[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/e0a7fd84e86681c7f356b6f1c7b500ded7a1a739.png[/img]
[i][h3]“But they’re not here yet… Prepare Defences!”[/h3][/i]
Defensive techniques will vary between Captains, but ultimately will come down to the utilisation of the same resources. There are some incredibly useful pieces of tech to be implemented from our Build Mode, as you can see in this clip from the Combat Trailer:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/f6d78de661d404b7c677801e6eb13d7707fe2bab.gif[/img]

[b]Weapon Lockers: [/b]these contain laser pistols (specifically BZ-pattern laser pistols, nicknamed ‘Buzzers') which the Marines in your Combat Division can equip to fend off invaders. Euphora isn’t afraid to grab one if the need arises either.

[b]Jumplight Memory Unit:[/b] this is an Engine Room upgrade that increasess the maximum Jumplight that your Jumplight Core can hold, allowing for even longer Jumps. Useful if you need to create some more breathing room between you and the Zutopan Fleet.

[b]Blast Doors: [/b]sturdy doors that have more health than regular doors, which will slow down the Zutopans trying to break through them. Blast Doors have the added benefit that they will seal shut as a safety precaution if they lose power, whereas your regular doors will be forced upon by a power outage.

[h3]The Captain’s Tools: Alert Levels[/h3]
Alert Levels are one of the main tools that the Captain can employ to encourage certain actions by the crew.

🟢 [b]Green Alert - All Clear!:[/b] An Active Green Alert is the standard for a normal day with regular operations in effect. Half of the crew will be on duty and will abide by a rotating shift. The other half are free to tend to their Needs, whether that be by socializing (flirting, maybe? ) or showering, eating, etc.

🟡 [b]Yellow Alert - All Hands to Your Stations!:[/b] When activated, Yellow Alerts will immediately place all crew On Duty. All operations are “normal”, but there are more hands ready to take on jobs. While Yellow Alert is active, no crew will partake in recreation or social activities (with a few exceptions – like our crew with the Chatterbox trait!), and they will not see to their Needs unless they are Critical.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/2d1464c4357703937972675e5a22b5a72c8b6db4.gif[/img]

🔴 [b]Red Alert - Battlestations! [/b]This is not a Drill!: As shown in the Combat Trailer! Activating a Red Alert will immediately force all crewmembers On Shift. All hands are ready to take jobs. 

[b]Red Alerts also activates:[/b]
[list][*] Officers and Captain assemble in the Bridge
[*] Marines operate Turrets and don spacesuits/helmets (if able - they protect against attacks from Zutopans!)
[*] Crews Assemble to the assigned Fighter Craft
[*] Crew members become Stressed, their default movement is to run
[*] There is no recreation or social, and no crew see to Needs unless critical[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/8dac99098235ca5eee3e3e44be6397d9e7843ed6.gif[/img]

⚫ [b]Black Alert - Emergency Hold!:[/b] Typically used when supplies are getting low, Black Alert imposes heavy rationing on all supplies. Crew will only eat, drink, wash and heal if their Need is Critical. Additionally, only Half of the Crew are On Duty (the shift still rotates).

🟣 [b]Magenta Alert - Intruder Alert!:[/b] For when you think there is something awry… Magenta Alert will call All Hands to Stand By, ready to receive jobs.

[b]Magenta Alerts also activates:[/b]
[list][*] Officers and Captain assemble in the Bridge
[*] Marines arm themselves with weaponry and don spacesuits/helmets
[*] Marines' receive a new set of priorities. First, to engage invaders. If Invaders are not present, Marines will operate Turrets. If there are no operable Turrets, Marines patrol the decks instead
[*] Crew members become Stressed, their default movement is to run
[*] Non-Marines assemble at Assembly Points, designated by you (as the Captain) as “Safe Zones”[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/898ab149abd922a262c14d4c5b9316550519ca32.gif[/img]

[i][h3]The Zutopans are Here![/h3][/i]
Once the Zutopan Boarding Pods have been detected, Combat is initiated. The Turrets will clock the Boarding Pods and attempt to shoot them down before they can attach to the ship itself.

Turrets are used by characters to defend the ship. Your crew will handle the shooting part – you don’t need to worry about that as the Captain. The turrets are able to protect the ship so long as they’re approaching the correct side, and the turrets have sufficient Munitions supplied.

Red alert will see Marines prioritize arming the Turrets and readying themselves for incoming threats. Magenta, rather, is used for combat tasks (they may still arm Turrets if the threat is present).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/06391352b8bb582ab7e4c3bb15ea07a6622005b2.gif[/img]

[i][h3]“Scramble Fighters!”[/h3][/i]
As a protective measure, the Captain is able to Scramble Fighters. The Fighters are manned by assigned crew members and will launch from the Flight Deck like any Away Mission, leaving to engage the Zutopans off-screen. While engaged against Zutopans, the Fighters are consuming Munitions, and must return to the Hangar to restock when they run dry.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/4afdf0af334c5d630eb5b49887f92bbb59d8ac14.gif[/img]

[h3]Combat Aboard the Catalina[/h3]
If the Boarding Pods successfully latch onto the Catalina, the Zutopan forces are able to board. Immediately, depending on your alert, the Marines will engage in Combat to protect the rest of the Crew, who will flee to the Assembly Zones. 

(It’s worth noting that you can pre-empt the combat and preserve your crew’s safety by initiating an Alert before the Zutopans actually reach the ship. If you can see the Pods approaching, it’s definitely a good time to go Red!)

The Marines will grab the nearest Pistol and suit up, if available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/beff982e138e2d59a4f9a22fae1b00fd77ed9f20.gif[/img]

The Marines are not well equipped to fend off a long-term Zutopan invasion. Preserving the Crew’s life, Morale and Hope (all of which are deeply linked) is a matter of evading the Zutopans as best as possible. With Blast Doors sealed, sometimes your best bet is to vent a room to vaccuum the majority of the Zutopan Forces out, even at the cost of some unlucky Crew.

Typically, Zutopan squards arrive in Boarding Parties which have a specific objective. It is primarily to find and destroy: whether that is the Captain (Princess Euphora) or the Jumplight Core in the Engine Room.

After breaching, the squad will move through the ship to reach their objective, blasting at any characters they encounter with pistols and destroying sealed doors that get in their way.

Your Marines will do their best – and will mobilize to equip themselves, then seek and engage the hostile Zutopans!

Non-Marines flee from enemies when they become aware of them.

[i][h3]“Not today, Voltan.”[/h3][/i]
Jumplight Odyssey is a story about survival above all else. The repercussions of engagement are severe – it causes Hope to dwindle, the Crew’s mood to drop and an impending resource drain. Combat feels more like being hit with a truck than something to willingly engage in – most moves on the SDF Catalina are made from a place of desperation to escape rather than combat dominance.

Once you Jump, you evade the clutches of the Zutopans and you live to fight another day. Anything you abandoned in the previous Star System remains lost as you move ever-onward, toward the Forever Star.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/20baf1d2eb11d10b725f568f831838edc3922867.gif[/img]

And that is a breakdown of our newest Combat Trailer, just in time for PC Gaming Show! We hope that you enjoy, and if you have any questions, feel free to let us know!


Until then!

Keeping your Hope Bars full,

<3 LoG

notes.title: Developer's Log #5: We Added Emojis ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
notes.content:
For the month of May, we’ve got a lil' MiniLog update that explores Jumplight Odyssey’s upcoming emoji system…

One of our big pain points in development has been trying to express the Needs of each crew member in a succinct and neat manner – a way that’s intuitive and wouldn’t interfere with the UI interface too severely. Said method needed to have enough weight to draw attention without causing clutter, be visually engaging and delightful in typical JLO fashion… 

Then inspiration struck!

Kind of like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/26c2887e8bdfa23fdf323c174847b4871dc64ccb.gif[/img]

💡Let’s draw from our anime roots and use similar visual cues!

In general, anime is renowned for its expressive and exaggerated character design. What we now recognise as emojis are skilfully integrated into the very art style and character design. From kaomojis to manpu, each symbol and detail represents a range of emotions that enhances storytelling, aids character development and often adds relatable comedic relief.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/40bb19a4992c98f9078f765d3ba38b049a82ddde.png[/img]

Most relevantly for us, though, the visual cues help viewers connect with the characters on a deeper level. It means that players can understand their crew member’s Moods without relying solely on clicking around the interface. Each of the lil' buddies is more human and tangible because you can see glimpses of how they’re feeling and what they need!

So, we got to work…

Our wonderful 2D Artist, Roger, sourced some emote icons. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/ee0f2911f2f605d3b67e92fd876509fcb6bd4d3b.png[/img]
Then, our Principal Artist, Jonathan, quickly ideated a little, wiggly bubble that hovers above the crew member’s head.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/7e9259d6054a0909c491cb0a76f5710b3d2d6c77.png[/img]

Our insanely talented VFX Artist Stephen then threw together some common emotes on what each crew member might need:

After a little bit more tweaking and a nice dab of polish, we have the final result…

notes.title: Developer's Log #4: Away Missions!
notes.content:
[i]Hello Spacefarers! 🌙[/i]

Our last Developer’s Log hinted at one of our proudest in-game features: Away Missions.

The clues that we gave were ominous enough… We said that “[i]things aren’t always easy, and in a survival situation, sometimes risks are vital for the survival of the greater good… Including the notorious Away Missions[/i]”.

So… What are Away Missions? Why are Away Missions? Who are Away Missions? :eye: :lips: :eye: 

Lettttt’ssss go!

[h2]What are Away Missions? Why are they important?[/h2]
With the SDF Catalina at your command, you will quickly realise that Away Missions are a vital part of the function of the ship. You can dispatch a spacecraft with personnel of your choosing to complete missions with varying degrees of risk – all with the objective of earning critical resources, rescuing stragglers, or a variety of other benefits to help keep the Catalina moving.

Without Away Missions, the Catalina would quickly run dry, the crew would despair and everything would hit the metaphorical fan (or perhaps [i]vent[/i] in this situation?)

[b]Ultimately, Away Missions are an integral part of our core game loop.[/b] You will engage with them after every jump in order to keep your ship stocked with all the goodies that you need to maintain your population and expand your capabilities. It’s also how you’ll bring new crew onto the ship, including some special rare finds.

They are so important that, in order to be a successful Captain, you’ll need to plot your route through the stars with them in mind. Do I take the long way to go via a resource-rich [i][b]Asteroid Field[/b][/i], knowing that the Zutopans will gain ground on me? Do I risk taking my ship to a molten-spewing [i][b]Fractured World[/b][/i], in search of the precious Metal found their in abundance? We expect the player to be making these sort of 'Captain’s calls' often. 

Away Missions, and the benefits they may bring, are at the heart of these decisions.

As they say…

[i][b]“Shoot for the moon. Even if you miss, you’ll land among the stars”[/b][/i]

Well, sort of. Heh.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/076e957bb1141fa4c8399f265ed9d8b807783455.png[/img]
Each of these missions will demand different things of the SDF Catalina -- whether this be crew, spacecraft, risk assessment levels and/or resource benefits. 

Some crew will be naturally better suited to certain mission types due to their Division membership and any special Callsign they may have!

[b]🔭 Scout Missions [/b]
[i]Gain Intel on Star System, learning its [i]Biome[/i] and Missions.[/i]

Different Biomes will hold different missions and resources. You'll need to plot your course carefully to make sure you can get the resources you need, when you need them. Need Biomass? Look for a [i]Verdant World[/i]. Low on water? Head to a [i]Frozen System[/i] to crack open a floating iceberg. 

Getting to know each Biome is a key skill for a Captain to master. Each Sector of space will contain different Biomes, meaning different opportunities. 

(We can chat about Sectors and Biomes in their own deepdive later…)


[b]📝 Survey Missions [/b]
[i]Reveal the yield of Resource Missions, expose hidden Salvage Missions.[/i]

Some missions (including juicy Salvage Operations) are hidden, so you'll need to spend time surveying for them. But don't forget; time spent surveying is more time for the Zutopans to catch up to you... The risk may be worth the reward... Sometimes. 

You'll need to decide how much you want to gamble on these.


[b]💧 Resource Extraction[/b]
Gain an amount of a given resources.

Resource extraction will send a crew to a potentially hazardous planet to collect valuable resources. The success of the mission depends on the skill and traits of the crew, the risk level accepted, the ship deployed and the player’s ability to navigate the risks and rewards of the extraction process.


[b]⛑ Rescue Extraction[/b]
Gain an amount of Civilians.

Much like Resource Extraction missions, Rescue Extraction are missions where the crew search for galactic stranded folks. Successfully returning with a new group of survivors is a sure-fire way to restoring a bit of Hope to those onboard.

You may be surprised by the results of some missions. A routine Rescue Operation may bring aboard a surprise character, for example. There's some nasty surprises to find out there in the cosmos too. Like what is that strange cough your pilot picked up on a Rescue Extraction mission? I wouldn't worry about it, I'm sure it's nothing.. 👀


[b]🛦 Combat Air Patrol:[/b]
[i]Gives early warning of threats for Combat Air Patrol response.[/i]

With Combat Air Patrol Missions, your crew are patrolling for any threats that may present themselves. Having this mission active will mean Combat is immediately responded to and there are no scrambling-related delays. The Patrol lasts until the craft are Recalled, or until the Fighter is out of Munitions.

We’ll speak to Combat in Jumplight Odyssey more in future Developer’s Logs!

… As well as the other types of Away Missions :wink:.

[h2]More on the Shuttles![/h2]
There are versatile spacecraft aboard the SDF Catalina. Some Spacecraft trade durability in favour of speed, and vice versa. Choosing your which Spacecraft to invest in will define your strategy; are you going slow for a bigger payload, or fast for a quick return?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/9178216908afa0002d73f59bb01bbad1adcb75cc.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/6810dddb918727a967dfd6fc6a5d8ff4492801db.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/e0fa7a003b0f9117493ec044123aab3bbd695dab.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/d929ab6b6b4ae5815cfbce85f715b4934fd4449d.png[/img]

[h2]Only the Bravest…[/h2]
Spacecraft need pilots. As captain, you'll be assigning a compliment of crew to each spacecraft, who will then depart with it on missions. The larger the craft, the larger the crew. This choice matters; each crew assigned will bring a bonus based upon their division (for example, Science Division members reduce damage dealt to all crew members). Furthermore, some crew have rare [i][b]Callsigns[/b][/i], acquired in the line of duty, which provide additional, impactful bonuses - and, occasionally, drawbacks too!

You can find out more very soon. After all, there's much, much (much much) more to come!

Until then…

notes.title: Developer's Log #3: Crew Relationships (Ooh, La La!)
notes.content:
[i]Hello Spacefarers![/i] 🌙

This Developer’s Log will give you a glimpse under the hood in all things Crew Needs & Relationships.

[b][i]As the Captain, it’s up to you to inspire your crew to stay focused on their mission and remind them of the importance of their roles in the face of constant danger.[/i][/b]

Building strong relationships with your crew members will be crucial to your success in Jumplight Odyssey. Each member of your team has their own unique personality and motivations that will affect their interactions with each other and with you. By investing time and effort into your crew, you'll not only improve their effectiveness in combat and survivability, but also create a more positive and cohesive environment onboard the ship.

Clearly it’s all in a day’s work for the Captain (that’s you!) to make sure everything else is running, too!

So get ready to embark on a perilous journey through the stars, where survival depends not only on the ship's systems, but on the bonds you forge with your crew.

Let’s explore how we put the [i]opera[/i] in [i]space opera[/i] in this Devlog..

[h2]The Intrinsic Nature of Hope…[/h2]
Hope is shown in the top bar of Jumplight Odyssey and is one of the most (if not, potentially [i][b]the[/b][/i] most) important resource for the Captain to manage. Generally, Hope indicates the population's psychological wellbeing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/c042e0144fad20941f1a45d7fe08e961a9c3e4e1.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/2d26ead84d8ed63b8d7ff5121026fc1dc57b5c3b.png[/img]

Hope ranges on a spectrum from “hopeful”, to “wavering” to “despairing” and, finally, “lost”. When Hope slips down, it results in knock-on effects among the entire ship. It also leads to a greater likelihood of [i][b]Disasters[/b][/i] occurring… 

There is a direct relationship between “Hope” and “Morale”. When Hope is high, it is able to pull characters out of the darkest depths of despair. When Hope is low, it drags them down. 

[h2]More on Morale![/h2]
Morale is a measure of the individual’s wellbeing. It embodies their current circumstances, any recent events that might affect them, and any influences that they’ve had. You can spot the “Morale” measure on the crewmate’s Character Profile.

You can also examine some other important features, like the crewmate’s Mood and Status. (Lil' note: this UI is a WIP and will probably be updated!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/fff88fbaab8939f619c55039267227f1394603a8.png[/img]

You know what, let’s follow a little crewmate along for their journey in a typical day on the SDF Catalina and see what shenanigans we encounter…

[h2]Tailing Aera![/h2]
Introducing Aera! If we head over to our Crew Manifest, a panel that captures data on everyone aboard the Catalina, we can see that Aera is currently in the [i][b]Engineering Division[/b][/i]! We can also pick up on useful information, like the fact they are [b]Bruised[/b] and probably should rest up or head to the Medical Bay soon!  

From the Manifest, we can also quickly see Aera’s outstanding [b]Needs[/b]. For full effectiveness on their behalf, they need more Socialisation (to fulfil [i]Lonely[/i]) and something to eat (to satisfy [i]Hungry[/i])! Engaging in relative activities, like playing chess with other crewmates or heading to the cafeteria, will help relieve these Needs.

At the bottom of the Crew Manifest, we can also see their current [b]Influences[/b]. These are important to note, but we’ll come back around to those in a later Dev Log. 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/cef4b191723a652f9d4ce7cd31d129d81dd75d80.png[/img]

If we cick “[i]Inspect Character[/i]”, we flick through to Aera’s Character Panel where we can find out a little more about them specifically…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/e37e87c0a6e5a5a5d30fae7e84cfc16633aa8163.gif[/img]

Here they’re going about their day aboard the SDF Catalina! Let’s see what kind of relationships they have aboard the ship. 

Ah! We can see they’re [i][b]Lovers[/b][/i] with Beki (ooh La La), but that relationship might not be unanimously shared… If we head to Beki’s Character Panel, we can see that Beki considers Aera an [i][b]Acquaintance[/b][/i]. The scandal!

If we do a bit more investigating, we can see Beki considers Saeron their [i][b]Bestie[/b][/i], but Saeron has a [i][b]Crush[/b][/i] on Beki.

It’s shaping up to be the scandalous love triangle here, with Beki at the peak…

The crew relationships in Jumplight Odyssey are affected by how your crew interact with other crewmates. The result of these interactions are also directly related to each crew member’s Mood.

Things aren’t always easy, and in a survival situation sometimes there are risks necessary to take for the greater good… Including the notorious [i][b]Away Missions[/b][/i].

(We plan to cover off on Away Missions in next month’s Devlog!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/f78180a5bab4ebfb105d215868efbf10dff31c63.gif[/img]

[h2]Disaster Strikes![/h2]
For now… Let’s mimic something disastrous happening and examine the consequences on Hope! I’m going to unseal some of the airlocks, which will depressurise and drain the oxygen out of the rooms… We’re going to cover this mechanic more specifically in another Devlog, but just know that this will cause  nearby folks to suffocate.

Once the crew begins to suffocate, you are notified and the Disaster begins to escalate. Hopefully, you can get it under control, but if you can’t… Well, you can see the results below:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/7bc10d306c8404bb7b961ce6c7e614e3cf073070.gif[/img]

Other than the frantic running and red flashing, the most obvious detriment is the slow decline of the [i][b]Hope Bar[/b][/i]. This mass casualty event draining Hope makes for a ripe situation where crew may become [i][b]Broken[/b][/i], which has disastrous consequences on its own… In the above GIF, you can see a Broken crew member has obtained the [i]Pyromaniac[/i] quirk… 

[i](We’ll explore quirks and personality traits in a later Devlog!)[/i]

Sometimes folks aboard the SDF Catalina don’t get the happy endings they deserve.. And that’s part of the balance the Captain has to constantly maintain. Those who have established relationships between Crew will experience despair when their friends and family are hurt, and when Hope on the Catalina is low.

… Except this guy, who seems to be having a great day despite the mass casualties onboard!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/f24f12236651923c8444c15fdf539d96e8899e98.gif[/img]

Each Crew Member has the opportunity for very unique, funny and exceptional experiences aboard the SDF Catalina! In Jumplight Odyssey, there is an equal focus on the gravity of the situation these folks find themselves in with the necessary melodrama of any good space opera.

[h2]Our Game Designer Jono explains…[/h2]
Basically crew will come aboard with some relationships from their former life, and will form new ones when interacting with each other! There are friendships, crushes, lovers, RIVALS AND NEMESES, and someone might not feel the same way about you as you do them!

Crew might start out on the wrong foot, and meet someone when they're in a grumpy or stressed out mood, forming a RIVALRY. This will worsen into a NEMESIS relationship if they keep meeting on such bad terms, but if things turn around and they have a lot of positive interactions, they could go from rivals to friends... [i]or lovers[/i]. 

If someone special to you like your lover dies, you'll take a huge morale hit and get all sad and gloomy, but if your rival dies you might even be HAPPIER for it. 

Today I saw a guy get knocked out, some science crew rushed to heal them, but they were in a stressed mood once they were revived, and shouted at the medical team who saved their life, making them into RIVALS.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/a01e99fd86bd3dd3b8f24e64f64faef64e12d048.gif[/img]

[h2]Wrapping Up[/h2]
We’re incredibly excited about how crew relationships are shaping up in Jumplight Odyssey. We know that building meaningful connections with your crew is just as important as escaping the enemies clutches, so we’re working hard to foster fun and creativity into each and every crew member.

With so many different folks to meet and interact with, there’s bound to be a few surprises along the way! (Like Beki’s love triangle?)

We can’t wait to see what kinds of relationships players will develop and how it might affect the journey to the Forever Star.

Catch us in the next Devlog, where we discuss [i][b]Away Missions[/b][/i]!

Until then…

[i]Keeping your Hope Bars full,[/i]

notes.title: Developer's Log #2: Breakdown of the Early Access Gameplay Teaser ⭐
notes.content:
[h1][i]Attention Spacefarers![/i][/h1]

For those who might have missed it, we recently released Jumplight Odyssey’s Gameplay Trailer as part of IGN’s Fan Fest…

[previewyoutube=WQQrpynKn9w;full][/previewyoutube]
To keep with the festive spirit, we thought that we could take you all through the :sparkles: details :sparkles: of the trailer itself to examine the development minutiae that may have been overlooked… :eyes: 

In doing so, we have some input by our wonderful Game Designer, Felix!

But first, of course, we highly recommend you hop into our [url=https://discord.com/invite/RZshTakzGp]Discord Server[/url], where our wonderful community discuss facets of the trailer themselves -- and some of their theories we are actually confirming right here in this Developer’s Blog...

[url=https://discord.com/invite/RZshTakzGp][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/04510b6fec84087a5fb0b204cadaa9fb4e2eb18a.png[/img][/url]


[h2]Shot #1: The SDF Catalina Exterior[/h2] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/9191a42e3ff1a92f2dc8154ee29b2395deb31c2a.png[/img]

A few community members have spied the [i][b]SDF Catalina’s point-defence system[/b][/i]… When crewed by military personnel, they are able to shoot down incoming threats before they can make an impact; whether that be incoming asteroids, torpedoes or boarding pods…

The SDF Catalina has a total of [i]8x 400mm Turbo Laser Cannons, 4x screening port and 4x screening starboard[/i], respectively.

A small detail ([i]that we’re surprised no one has picked up on![/i]) is the planet in the background in this screenshot. This featured planet is referred to as “[i][b]Tomb World[/b][/i]” in-game, but its ecosystem is entirely dead and barren, except for a few, small ruins of what may have been life… This is just one of the many planets available that are perfect for Resource Extraction – you gotta' fuel up to get to the Forever Star, after all!


[h2]Shot #2: The Bridge[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/121ec84fac588ca1b97a3e1ca21407d1a6d977f9.png[/img]

Here, we have the Bridge! The Bridge is the heart and command centre of your ship. 

It’s here that your officers and captain will report during High Alert Levels. It also houses critical stations for commanding and augmenting the capabilities of your four divisions; [i][b]Science, Combat, Engineering[/b][/i] and [i][b]Supply[/b][/i]. 

You will want to keep those running, for sure.

You will be able to build various upgrade modules to the Bridge, with a myriad of benefits - but, be warned, space is very limited! With all your things crammed into the hull of a Starship, managing space will be one of the hardest decisions you will have to make in Jumplight Odyssey!

There are also a number of command interfaces the player can interact with from the Bridge… [i]More to come on this in a future Developer’s Log.[/i] :eyes: 

Lastly, its from the Bridge that the player can initiate the [i][b]Jumplight Drive[/b][/i], readying the ship to jump!


[h2]Shot #3: A Unique Quality of Life Onboard...[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/59d8b81ba4c6d0f6fac11dd306f6a3afb35c588e.png[/img]

It is integral to Jumplight Odyssey that all events and mechanics – while overdramatized enough to be in a soapbox drama – are realistic! It’s important for us to get a sense of tactility in the simulation of our ship, its crew and the objects they use. After asking our Game Designer, Felix, “how hard is linking realism, animations, moods, pressurisation and any other situation you can think of?”, they responded with:

[i]*cries in dev*[/i]

Mood.

[quote=Felix, JLO Game Designer]“Serious answer though; it’s tough. We have a very large population of characters whom we simulate very physically, and who can be affected by all manner of things in real time. It’s a big investment on our time and efforts, but bringing our crew authentically to life is important to us. This is ultimately a leadership sim where you are entrusted to lead the people around you; we need the people you are leading to feel real.”[/quote]
Ultimately, Characters in JLO have relationships and also have several needs that they need to satisfy in order to remain healthy and happy. One of these is [i][b]Socialisation[/b][/i]. These relationships can develop and shift over the course of their journey. Who a character talks to and how each of them are feeling when they do so are both important parts of the simulation!

More to come in a future Developer’s Log about [i][b]Crew Relationships[/b][/i]!


[h2]Shot #4: Panic! Aboard the Ship...[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/9042b54f099efc4aa045222d045cbb3c7cd6e9ab.png[/img]

[i][b]Alert Levels [/b][/i]are actually controlled by the Catalina’s Captain – you! You will be responsible for selecting the adequate Alert Level for the situation your crew finds themselves in. The Alert Levels are one of the most effective ways of getting your entire crew to jump into gear!

There are several varied Alert Levels you can initiate, each with their own protocol for the crew to observe.

But not without consequences… Going into high alert levels will stress characters out, which can wreck havoc on their moods and - by extension - their relationships. Not to mention that when characters are responding to alert levels, they won’t be able to see to their needs… 

Without their needs met, characters will suffer, which will in turn cause Hope to dwindle… It’s a vicious cycle downward from here!

So much for a Captain to balance... 😅


[h2]Shot #5: "Hope is a Waking Dream" - Aristotle[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/2bcd6bc20b499bbcee33cd66827b4c3dbb7a2a5e.png[/img]

In JLO, Hope is what keeps the darkness at bay. It has an effect on each and every characters' emotional wellbeing (called [i][b]Morale[/b][/i] in game). With certain decisions, you can raise your crew’s spirits (when Hope is high) or bring this spirit down (when Hope is low). 

Each character's Morale is individually simulated, but Hope is shared. It’s a resource you’ll need to keep a close eye on.

([i]There's more to come in a future Developer’s Log about the importance of Hope![/i])

One thing that we are able to hint at for now is how Jumplight Odyssey’s music expresses Hope, or… How Hope is expressed through changes in music.

Our Game Designer, Felix, explained it like this:

[quote]We tie music to Hope as a way of capturing the ‘vibe’ of the ship. Are people feeling optimistic? Have some sweet space-lounge! Are people feeling grim? Play that morose trumpet, baby!

It’s important to us that the player’s emotions are tied to the wellbeing of their population. Music is an incredibly powerful tool to convey human emotion, so it’s a wonderful way to have JLO reflect Hope back to the player![/quote]


[h2]Shot #6: Away Missions... 🚀[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/e23151fd4fdca6cf7bec14c7ac93d96799e5bb42.png[/img]

Our Game Designer, Felix, briefly explores the potential in JLO’s Away Missions:

[quote]Every star system you visit has the potential for Away Missions. With these, you’ll be able to extract resources or rescue people, bringing them aboard as civilians or - if they are trained already - fully fledged crew. 

The Away Missions available in each star system will vary depending on the biome you are in. Don’t expect a lot of civilians waiting for you at a Blackhole, for example.

Away Missions can serve a few other purposes, helping with intel and defence - but we’ll talk more about that when we have more substantial things to share![/quote]
Future Developer’s Log content mayhaps? :eyes: 

All that we will add here is that the specific ship you are viewing in this screenshot is an [i][b]Orion Class Shuttle[/b][/i]!


[h2]Shot #7: Just keep building, building, building...[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/162f36453263370c986dcb80fe5ecadec0f1a4ab.png[/img]

As we mentioned before, one of your greatest commodities onboard the Catalina is space. At some point, with all the functions you require for maintaining the ship and crew, you will likely run out of space. This may mean you need to deconstruct and retool your rooms.

Felix helpfully provided the example that:

[quote]You may gear your ship towards resource processing while you’re in the resource-rich ‘Mineral Ring’ Sector (we’ll talk more on Sectors later), then later deconstruct those resource processing objects for parts later on so the resources can be put to use elsewhere.[/quote]
In doing so, you find, shape and utilise the resources that you’ll need to survive what’s ahead effectively. 

While making use of Away Missions is essential for gathering resources and recruits, ultimately you’ll always have your next Jump in mind. The Zutopan fleet isn’t going to sit ideally by and wait for all your mining operations to complete!


[h2]Shot #8: Careers Aboard the Catalina![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/8e6df0e7c68d0bc7a5c6f8a8629de4149f8dc539.png[/img]

There are currently four divisions; [i][b]Science, Engineering, Supply[/b][/i] and [i][b]Combat[/b][/i]. Deciding which crew member goes where is largely up to the Captain, but it is worth keeping in mind the specific traits of the entire crew…

More to come here. 😉


[h2]Shot #9: About the Mizzi Manoeuvre[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/f3592a08d5bc18a693638017b64840a01223dd52.png[/img]

[i](Bonus Points if you read our previous Developer’s Log and know what the Mizzi Maneouvre is!)[/i]

As funny as it appears, sending crew into space actually does serve a function onboard the ship. Venting the air out of a room is a very useful way of quickly extinguishing fires – which require oxygen to burn.

Of course, if the crew haven’t gotten clear, you may lose one ([i]or two… Or five, like in this trailer[/i]).


[h1]And so much more to come![/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/7cc0210903923f2a27a773cffc4387947866e40c.png[/img]

The last part of the trailer captures a lot of what is yet to be announced! Greenhouses, the Galley, interactions between crew members – all of these are facets we’re working heavily on.

In the future, we’re planning for more! More things! All the things to come!

But all of that will have to wait until the next Developer’s Log...

Keeping your Hope Bars Full,
:heart: LoG
