notes.title: Developer's Log #1: 2022 Wrapped, Lighting & Plants! 🌱
notes.content:
[i][h1]Attention Spacefarers![/h1][/i]

As always, we hope that you have had a wonderful, restful holidays. 💫

With Jumplight Odyssey’s first DevLog ([i]Or Captain’s Log, maybe? … OK, yep, working title[/i]), we thought that we would not only wrap up everything that’s happened over the last year, but take a peek in the Engine Room ([i]Another working title – Gosh, so cheesy[/i]) for JLO’s future development.

Although, before we jump in, introductions are in order… We’ve onboarded a Community Manager ([i]Psst – Hi! That’s me![/i]). Chan (She/Her) will be the best point of contact for the League of Geeks community to connect with the Dev Team.. Including releasing regular Developer Updates, just like this one.

You can also come hang out with her ([i]and the rest of our pals[/i]) on our [url=https://discord.gg/RZshTakzGp][i][b]Official League of Geeks Discord Server[/b][/i][/url]!

Now, onto the Devlog! 

…

For this Devlog, we’ve asked Blake, our awesome Studio Design Director, and Game Director, to hop in and answer a few questions.

[h1]2022 FOR JUMPLIGHT ODYSSEY: WRAPPED[/h1]
[h3]I’m New Here! What is Jumplight Odyssey?[/h3]

Jumplight Odyssey plays as a retro Sci-Fi survival colony sim with a small dash of management sim. You take on the role of Princess Euphora, a much-loved leader and last Regent, tasked with leading her people to the Forever Star – the colony’s sanctuary. With their homeland destroyed, your people are relying on you to manage the crew, control the ship’s systems and – most importantly – to keep hope alive!

[previewyoutube=mitPu7bcDB8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Cool. What inspired this project? It’s not the same as your other titles..[/h3]
The project is inspired by a few ideas that all crashed together. For my part, I grew up as a kid watching and loving Robotech, and always wanted to make a game exploring the anguish and stress the crew were under while managing a space battlecrusier. Cut to me being an adult with the ability to make that dream a reality…

Over the last few years, there have been some insanely cool management sims released: Fallout Shelter, Rimworld, FTL, Two Point Hospital, Evil Genius, just to name a few. I also had a collection of all these new Star Wars Incredible Cross Section books. The idea was to create a true mecca of all these ideas in a big melting pot. 

Ty, our Creative Director, had the brilliant idea to drop the Robotech influence and push the aesthetic further back to retro anime - think StarBlazers. I think a liiiiittle part of me died at the time, but I can now really appreciate the change. Jumplight Odyssey feels much fresher for its aesthetic, and we’re proud to say that it truly stands apart from what other studios are working on.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/7e05b478c5836ece5fed2f1c780dc4a1843c5b95.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/1bf30c63e6cb874609caf43e22a01125a07c8c9a.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/c3230433caf6e69e3039f6130137899b3a4f2910.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]

[h3]What niche does Jumplight Odyssey fill that was previously underserved? [/h3]
People love space, people love space sims – many are wonderful, but many more are heavy or very clunky. I enjoyed the lightness of Two Point Hospital and wanted to combine it with the emergent events of Rimworld (and the Grand Daddy Dwarf fortress). With Jumplight Odyssey, we are seeking to find a nice balance where we can deliver a focus on crew mechanics that other sims lack. 

That's part of League of Geek's special sauce, we look at opportunities and see if we can do something really special, and take it further than anyone else is right now. 

Jumplight Odyssey also has a heart to it. We're pouring a lot of ourselves into this game. There's charm, warmth, clumsiness, humour and sadness – sometimes all within a few moments – but it has a spirit that I think most players will fall in love with.

Also did you want to manage a space battlecruiser in a 1970s retro future sci-fi adventure across the stars? Do you want to play it while absorbing the tunes of 1970's Tokyo late night disco jazz? 

We got you covered. 👾

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/5fb362fd3d0c0f8a7836acdbcb1d03ee13241620.gif[/img]

[h1]ON TO THE FUTURE![/h1]
Last year, we focused on building out the bones of what we wanted to see in Jumplight Odyssey. We built in the building core mechanics, infrastructure, features for the system and ideated the basic lore. Of course, with any colony sim and management game, there’s always a massive amount to do.

We’re taking reasonable time to get the details right – the Art Department have since done some amazing work on improving the lighting models, shaders and textures. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/237d53e3461e4945ff4ca1cec26f939c97a33936.png[/img]

It’s very common knowledge that the biggest focus on any ship – seafaring or spacefaring – is safety. This has also been our focus, especially what would happen in the event of a disaster. We’re keepings things as realistic as possible, including O2 and airflow in the ship. 

Just a few examples of that are..
[list][*] You can depressurise rooms if you want to open an airlock ([i]WARNING: this will shoot your crew straight into space! This is called the Mizzi Manoeuvre, because Blake loves to space his crew for fun[/i])
[*] Fire will only function in oxygenised rooms (and will also consume said oxygen)
[*] Plants create oxygen [/list]
In Jumplight, we want all the simulating systems to become toys for the player to use, experiment with, manipulate, leverage and push against in their playthroughs.

And for all our farming sim fiends, we’ve got you covered. As you can see below, we’ve got our Greenhouses up and running. This part of the ship is filled with plants, herbs and growing food – all functioning as an integral part of everyday life on Jumplight Odyssey. Many folks on our team are Green-thumbs and are pouring their love and soul into these little planty bois.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43221983/9d997955b149704f5265dea06deb2021dbe45939.gif[/img]

There’s so much more to say, but we’re going to have to wait for the next devlog! Tune in next February for some more delightful hints and peaks.

Keeping your Hope Bars full,

League of Geeks :heart:
